title: Jude and the Choir
premise: Coral Dunmore has spent twenty-six years in the valley of Hollowmere, where an old covenant suppresses magic and keeps its residents invisible to the world beyond—including to the prophecy-books that record every soul's fate. When a date named Jude arrives for a blind date, Coral finds their evening already written in a century-old prophetic text, down to the words they will say. The book reveals that Hollowmere was erased from existence by a dying king's spell, and that Coral's beast-speech is the key to reopening the door out—but every attempt costs a memory. As Jude, who is not what they seem, and Coral grow closer, they must decide whether truth or loyalty to the valley's comfortable lie matters more. In the end, Coral speaks the door open at the cost of forgetting Jude entirely, walks out into the real country, and must choose whether to trust a stranger who claims they once loved each other.
about_author: Silas Joubert is the pen name of a former choir director from the Karoo who traded hymnals for folklore after finding his grandmother's hand-copied prophecy book in a locked piano bench. He writes fantasy about small towns, large silences, and the price of being remembered.

chapters.title: The Valley That Isn't
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral tends goats and hides their beast-speech on the morning of a blind date arranged by their meddling aunt. Establishes Hollowmere's suffocating coziness and the rule that no one leaves. Emotional beat: restless longing disguised as contentment.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Gate
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Jude arrives—charming, wrong-footed, asking odd questions about roads that don't exist. Their date is awkward and electric. Coral notices animals go silent around Jude. Emotional beat: first spark of connection shadowed by unease.

chapters.title: What the Crows Said
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A crow warns Coral that 'the paper man is here.' Coral dismisses it, but that night finds their aunt burning papers. Emotional beat: denial curdling into suspicion; the gift Coral buried begins whispering again.

chapters.title: The Book in the Piano Bench
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude searches the chapel and finds a prophecy book dated 1899 containing tonight's date verbatim—including Coral's exact words. Jude's secret mission is hinted. Emotional beat: guilt, because Jude knew before arriving.

chapters.title: Written Before We Met
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Coral catches Jude with the book; confrontation becomes confession—their whole evening is transcribed, including lines neither has said yet. Emotional beat: terror of predestination, and intimacy born of shared fear.

chapters.title: Hollowmere, Population Forgotten
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The book reveals Hollowmere was erased by King Aldric's dying spell—a country within a country, hidden so thoroughly even its people forgot. Emotional beat: grief for a self that was stolen without consent.

chapters.title: The Aunt Who Knew
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Aunt Verity admits she found the book decades ago and chose silence to protect everyone. Mother-daughter-style rupture between Coral and the woman who raised her. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth made flesh in one kitchen argument.

chapters.title: Beast-Speech Is Treason
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Flashback chapters via Jude's orders: outside the valley, beast-speakers are hunted because they can command the door-guardians. Jude was sent to verify Coral is the one. Emotional beat: Jude falling for the person they were sent to use.

chapters.title: The Choir Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Town choir practice becomes eerie—everyone sings a hymn no one taught them, and the lyrics are instructions for staying forgotten. Coral realizes the valley maintains itself through them. Emotional beat: horror wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: First Memory Gone
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral experiments with speaking to the valley's stone guardian; it works, but Coral loses the memory of their mother's face. Emotional beat: the true cost revealed—not death, but erosion.

chapters.title: Jude's Confession
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude tells Coral everything: the order they serve, the hunt for beast-speakers, and that leading Coral out may mean handing them to it. Emotional beat: betrayal offered honestly, love offered anyway.

chapters.title: Verity's Bargain
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Aunt Verity tries to strike a deal with the guardian herself to spare Coral, revealing she once tried to leave—and lost her husband to the price. Emotional beat: protective lies reframed as scar tissue.

chapters.title: The Road That Was Never Built
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Coral and Jude map the erased country using the prophecy book's marginalia, discovering the door lies beneath the chapel where the choir sings. Emotional beat: purpose replacing paralysis; the pair become conspirators.

chapters.title: Neighbors With Knives
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The town senses the plan; neighbors who feel like family turn watchful, then hostile—the valley defending its own forgetting. Emotional beat: loyalty inverted into menace.

chapters.title: The Hymn Has Teeth
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Trapped in the chapel, Jude hears the choir's song rewrite his memories of his orders, trying to make him forget why he came. He fights it by reciting Coral's name. Emotional beat: memory as resistance.

chapters.title: What Coral Chose to Forget
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. To open the door fully, Coral must give up the memory dearest to them. They secretly rehearse letting go of Jude. Emotional beat: quiet devastation; love measured in advance of loss.

chapters.title: The Night of the Door
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Beneath the chapel, Coral commands the guardians open while the town converges above. Verity holds the choir off with the truth shouted aloud. Emotional beat: climax—courage, sacrifice, the door groaning wide.

chapters.title: Out
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral steps into the real country—vast, loud, unhidden—and turns to find Jude, but the price has been paid: Coral doesn't know him. Emotional beat: hollow triumph; freedom with a hole in it.

chapters.title: The Stranger Who Cries
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude follows Coral out, now a stranger to them, and must decide whether to tell the truth or walk away. He chooses truth, offering the prophecy book as evidence. Emotional beat: humility; love without claim.

chapters.title: Reading Ourselves Again
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral reads their own handwriting in the margins—notes past-Coral left as insurance: 'Trust the sad man with the book.' Emotional beat: tentative re-beginning built on evidence rather than feeling.

chapters.title: The Hunt Finds the Door
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Jude's order arrives at the opened door; Coral's beast-speech turns the valley's guardians outward to hold the line. Verity's fate is revealed—she stayed by choice, keeper of the threshold. Emotional beat: the cost of power confronted head-on.

chapters.title: A Country With Room For Us
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Epilogue months later: Coral, no longer hiding, teaches beasts' names to children in the real country; Jude waits each day to be remembered or chosen anew. Coral chooses him—again, freely. Emotional beat: resolution—memory lost, love rebuilt by choice.
